ai.title: Add desktop.eventloophealth analytics event
ai.summary: New `DESKTOP_EVENT_LOOP_HEALTH` enum value added to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. This event tracks saturation of the orchestrator's single event loop, which serves the renderer bundle, SSE streams, git work, agent turns, terminals, and preview drives. The data distinguishes backend queuing from local orchestrator pinning, addressing recent reports of slow tab opening.

eli5.text: When you open a new tab or use any feature in the app, that action travels through one central pathway inside the software. New monitoring was added so the team can now see whether that pathway is getting backed up, which helps explain why some people noticed tab opening felt slow. You won't see this directly, but it lets the developers figure out if the app is slowing down because of its own internal traffic or because something else is waiting. The tracking is now in place, so the next time someone reports slowness, the logs can check whether this central pathway was overloaded.

ai.title: Basher short-circuits small command outputs before LLM summarization
ai.summary: The basher agent in agents/basher.ts now returns raw command output without an LLM step when the combined stdout, stderr, and message length is at most 2000 characters. This skips the summarization round-trip for ordinary command output, which the inline comment notes sits on the critical path of every typecheck and test spawn. The threshold constant RAW_OUTPUT_PASSTHROUGH_CHARS is defined inside handleSteps because the generator is serialized with toString and re-evaluated standalone, so it cannot close over module scope.
ai.evidence: In agents/basher.ts, handleSteps now computes rawChars as the sum of the lengths of the output object's stdout, stderr, and message fields, and when that total is under RAW_OUTPUT_PASSTHROUGH_CHARS (defined inline as 2000) and stdoutOmittedForLength is not set, it yields set_output with the raw output and includeToolCall false instead of yielding STEP to trigger an LLM summarization pass.

changes.what: handleSteps now returns raw output without an LLM step when the output object's stdout, stderr, and message lengths total at most 2000 characters, unless stdoutOmittedForLength is set.

ai.title: Add flake-hunt documentation and CI workflow details
ai.summary: Docs/testing.md adds a guide for `scripts/flake-hunt.ts`, a harness that reproduces CI flakes by running tests concurrently under CPU load. It details three common defects: hardcoded port collisions, polling instead of event listening, and timers leaking across tests. The section explains how to invoke the script with custom rounds and concurrency, and notes the weekly `flake-hunt.yml` workflow runs it against `freebuff-desktop` without blocking PRs.

eli5.text: When tests pass on a quiet computer but fail on a busy one, the problem is not the machine, it is the test hiding a real bug that load only exposes. A new troubleshooting guide explains how to reproduce those conditions on purpose by running tests many times at once while fake CPU work competes for resources, then lists the three most common hidden defects to look for: two runs talking over each other through a fixed connection point, waits that guess at timing instead of listening for the real signal, and background work from one test leaking into another. When you read it, the difference is concrete: a single test that looks fine on its own will start failing in groups, and the output will name exactly which assertions broke and under what load.

ai.title: docs/testing.md: shared-state flake patterns
ai.summary: Added documentation describing two shared-state test flakes found in the `cli` package. Root cause was tests writing to fixed paths (`__dirname/temp-test-images` and `os.tmpdir()/codebuff-test-*`) causing race conditions when run in parallel. Fix involves using unique `mkdtemp` directories per test run. CI masked these issues by isolating package suites, affecting only local dev and this harness.

eli5.text: If you run a certain group of tests side by side on your computer, they sometimes trip over each other and fail for no clear reason, even though each test passes when run alone. The problem happened because those tests were all trying to write their temporary files to the same shared folders on disk, so when two tests ran at the same time, they would overwrite or delete each other's data. The fix gives each test run its own private folder to work in, so they no longer collide, meaning those flaky failures should disappear when you run tests locally.

ai.title: Add desktop.featureused analytics event
ai.summary: New `DESKTOP_FEATURE_USED` enum value added to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts` to track long-tail desktop feature adoption. The event is added to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` in `common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts`, bypassing sampling to ensure accurate unique-user metrics for rare features. Volume control relies on intent-only emission and per-session deduplication rather than statistical sampling.

eli5.text: The app now tracks which desktop features people actually open and use, like panels, worktrees, diffs, skills, terminal, or preview, through a single new event called 'feature used'. This lets the product team see in one view what's popular and what's not, without creating a separate tracking entry for every new feature. Because the team serves roughly 1,000-2,000 daily users, any rare feature could be used by so few people that random sampling would record zero usage; the system avoids that by always counting these events and instead controls volume by only recording when you intentionally choose a feature and by remembering which features it already counted during your current session.

ai.title: docs/testing.md: CI fan-out, typecheck lanes, sdk cache
ai.summary: docs/testing.md adds a section explaining CI wall-clock halving (10m40s to 5m29s) by removing needs: edges from ci.yml and splitting typecheck from build-web. It documents typecheck-lanes.ts, which derives lanes at runtime because bun 1.3.14 ignores negated --filter arguments, and warns that missing lanes or unmatched filters exit 0 silently. sdk/dist caching via build-sdk action lacks restore-keys to prevent stale SDKs, and freebuff/web now honors SDK_ALREADY_BUILT. The doc notes freebuff-desktop thread-engine.test.ts is the heaviest suite but not on the critical path, and that per-job dependency cache restore (~40s) is now the floor.

eli5.text: The project added a guide explaining how its automated checks run faster by splitting one big pre-check step into separate typechecking and web-building jobs that now run in parallel, roughly cutting the total time from eleven minutes to under six. The guide also notes which slow tasks are unavoidable setup costs (like waiting for dependency caches) rather than the actual tests, and records a few silent-failure traps in the tooling that can make a fast-feeling build still miss checking new code or run against an outdated software-development kit if a future job isn't configured to either rebuild or explicitly reuse the pre-built one.

ai.title: docs/testing.md: baseline staleness and flaky suite annotations
ai.summary: docs/testing.md adds guidance on periodic baseline refresh, noting a 307-test gap in `freebuff-desktop` where CI stayed green despite missing tests. New `Flag retried tests` step emits `Flaky suite` warning annotations for pass-on-retry cases. Docs also warn that `Suite ran no tests` is now annotated for empty suites like `test:.agents`, and baselines for DB-backed suites must be recorded from CI runs to account for skipped test count discrepancies.

eli5.text: The change is live today for teams running the automated test suite that guards against silent test loss. If you maintain such a suite, you'll now see a "Flaky suite" warning appear on the run page whenever a test that failed on its first attempt passes when retried (the system still retries automatically, but no longer does so in silence), and you'll see a "Suite ran no tests" warning when a configured job selects no test files at all (for example a job pointing at a directory that doesn't exist yet). These warnings replace a previously green-without-reason status, so the concrete thing you notice is a yellow annotation calling out flakiness or empty runs instead of a clean green pass that hid the problem.

ai.title: Added desktop.turnbackgroundwait analytics event
ai.summary: Added DESKTOP_TURN_BACKGROUND_WAIT event to distinguish background command waits from unexplained stalls. Background Bash waits emit no stream messages, causing the stall detector to misclassify them as hangs. This event ensures long waits are counted while keeping desktop.turn_stalled reserved for true hangs. Added to ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS in analytics-sampling.ts to prevent sampling loss for rare signals.

eli5.text: When the assistant sends a command to run quietly in the background (like installing a package), you'll see it sitting there doing nothing for a while, that pause is now logged as a normal part of how long the command takes, not mistaken for the app freezing. The developers fixed this so their crash-detection system no longer thinks these expected waits are errors. If you ever look at usage stats, these background waits will now be counted separately from real problems. This is live in the latest version.
